analysis.title: Markets On The Move - APAC Equity Outflows Resume; EURUSD Offered, Gold Bid Into FOMC
key_insights: Asia cash equity flows are net sell-skewed in most markets: Japan 62% better to sell, Hong Kong/China 62% to sell (including 1% in shorts), Taiwan 67% sellers, ASEAN 61% better to sell. Australia is the exception at 63% buy skewed.
Nikkei 225 is up 1.2% on an AI/semiconductor rally. The desk is selling banks and trading companies and buying electric utilities and industrials.

KOSPI is up over 6% and near three-week highs. Foreign investors bought $580 mn and local institutions bought $360 mn in technology ahead of Microsoft and Google earnings and the FOMC decision. UBS sees foreign seller exhaustion after $14 bn of tech selling month to date.

TAIEX reclaimed its 60-day moving average at 46394 on below-normal turnover, with investors on the sidelines ahead of key tech earnings. The desk is better selling semiconductor bluechips and testing and thermals, and buying mature foundry.

EURUSD saw strong hedge fund selling below 1.1130 after breaking 1.1160 technical support. UBS expects it to hold around 1.1100 in Asia absent a major shock. Month-end corporate flows are likely to dominate direction through Wednesday.

Gold stabilized as reserve manager buying below 4,010 absorbed heavy speculative selling. UBS keeps a mildly bearish bias below 4,080-4,085 into the FOMC, with support at 4,025-4,030. The desk prefers tactical positioning and avoids aggressive shorts on a break above 4,085.
earnings_insights: Microsoft and Google earnings are cited as upcoming catalysts for Korean technology buying. No figures are given.
Taiwan investors are on the sidelines ahead of key tech earnings. Names and figures are not given.
